title: RNA isolation with TRIzol
author: Magdalena Julkowska
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.pbndime
materials: Discard the supernatant with a pipette
Determine RNA concentration using the nanodrop

steps.title: Lyse Tissue with TRIzol
steps.instruction: Add TRIzol to the tissue material and incubate to dissociate nucleoproteins.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 ml of TRIzol per 30-50 mg of tissue material

steps.title: Phase Separation
steps.instruction: Add chloroform to the lysate and centrifuge to separate phases.

substeps.instruction: Add 0.2 mL of chloroform per 1 mL of TRIzol Reagent used for lysis
Centrifuge the sample for 15 minutes at max speed at room temperature

steps.title: RNA Precipitation
steps.instruction: Isolate the aqueous phase and precipitate the RNA using isopropanol.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the aqueous phase containing the RNA to a new tube
Add 0.5 mL of isopropanol to the aqueous phase per 1 mL of TRIzol Reagent used for lysis
Centrifuge for 10 minutes at max speed at room temperature

steps.title: RNA Wash
steps.instruction: Wash the RNA pellet with ethanol.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of 75% ethanol per 1 mL of TRIzol used for lysis
Centrifuge for 5 minutes at max speed at room temperature

steps.title: Drying and Final Resuspension
steps.instruction: Dry the RNA pellet and resuspend it in RNase-free water.

substeps.instruction: Vacuum or air dry the RNA pellet for 5–10 minutes
Resuspend the pellet in 20–50 µL of RNase-free water by pipetting up and down
